topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: interplay of genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual foundations of cancer development through intrinsic genetic mutations, microenvironmental factors, environmental exposures, and stochastic processes.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and infectious mechanisms of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive tumorigenesis through inflammation and immune disruption, illustrated by the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and promotional carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation, chemical carcinogens, metabolic activation, and tumor promoters cause DNA damage and drive tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for detecting mutational signatures and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and assess cancer risk.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the final summary and closing remarks of the lecture.
